---
title: "REM16 and FT1 expression by plant sex in Cannabis"
output: html_document
---

## Purpose

This script takes an RNA-seq expression table (genes in rows, samples in columns)
and produces three box plots comparing female (XX) and male (XY) plants:

1. REM16 expression by plant sex
2. FT1 expression by plant sex
3. REM16 and FT1 side by side, with sex clearly identified

**How to run:** open this file in RStudio and click *Knit*, or run
`rmarkdown::render("<path to this file>")` from R. See `README.md` for setup.

**Inputs:** `Question_3/2_Data_RNASeq_Cannabis_Sex.csv` (already in the repo).

**Outputs:** three PNG files written to the `figures/` folder at the repo root.

## 1. Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
# --- Check dependencies first ---------------------------------------------
# Fail early with a clear, actionable message instead of a cryptic
# "there is no package called ..." error halfway through the script.
required_packages <- c("tidyverse", "here")
missing_packages  <- required_packages[!required_packages %in% rownames(installed.packages())]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing R package(s): ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "), ".\n",
    "Install them once with: install.packages(c(",
    paste0('"', missing_packages, '"', collapse = ", "), "))",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

library(tidyverse)  # data wrangling (dplyr, tidyr, stringr) and plotting (ggplot2)
library(here)       # builds file paths from the repo root, so no machine-specific paths
```

## 2. Settings (the only part you should ever need to edit)

```{r settings}
# Paths are built from the repo root with here(), so they work on any computer.
input_file <- here("Question_3", "2_Data_RNASeq_Cannabis_Sex.csv")
output_dir <- here("figures")

# Genes to analyse: names are the labels used in plots, values are the
# gene IDs exactly as written in the first column of the data file.
# NOTE: REM16 is stored with a "Cannabis_" prefix in this dataset while FT1 is
# not. We map the IDs here instead of renaming rows in the data, so the
# inconsistency is documented in one visible place.
target_genes <- c(
  REM16 = "Cannabis_LOC115699937",
  FT1   = "LOC115696989"
)

# Colour-blind-friendly colours (Okabe-Ito palette), one per plant sex.
# Names must match the sex labels created in section 4.
sex_colors <- c("Female (XX)" = "#D55E00", "Male (XY)" = "#0072B2")
```

## 3. Import and check the data

```{r import}
# Stop with a helpful message if the data file is missing, e.g. if the
# script is run from a copy of the repo that lacks the data.
if (!file.exists(input_file)) {
  stop(
    "Input file not found: ", input_file, "\n",
    "Check that the repo was cloned completely and that the file is in ",
    "the Question_3 folder.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

# The first column (gene IDs) has no header in the CSV, so read_csv() gives it
# a placeholder name. We rename it by POSITION (column 1) to "gene_id".
rnaseq_raw <- read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename(gene_id = 1)

# Assumption: every column other than gene_id is one sample, and its name
# ends in "_XX" (female) or "_XY" (male). Warn if any column breaks that rule,
# because those samples cannot be assigned a sex and will be excluded below.
sample_columns <- setdiff(names(rnaseq_raw), "gene_id")
unrecognised   <- sample_columns[!str_detect(sample_columns, "_(XX|XY)$")]

if (length(unrecognised) > 0) {
  warning(
    "These columns do not end in _XX or _XY and will be excluded: ",
    paste(unrecognised, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```

## 4. Extract the target genes and reshape to long format

```{r reshape}
# Keep only the rows for our genes of interest.
target_rows <- rnaseq_raw %>%
  filter(gene_id %in% target_genes)

# Each gene must appear exactly once. A missing gene (typo in the ID) or a
# duplicated row would silently give wrong plots, so check explicitly.
missing_genes <- setdiff(target_genes, target_rows$gene_id)
if (length(missing_genes) > 0 || nrow(target_rows) != length(target_genes)) {
  stop(
    "Expected exactly one row for each of: ",
    paste(target_genes, collapse = ", "), ".\n",
    "Found ", nrow(target_rows), " row(s). Missing: ",
    ifelse(length(missing_genes) == 0, "none (so an ID is duplicated)",
           paste(missing_genes, collapse = ", ")),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

# "Long" format = one row per gene per sample, which is what ggplot2 expects.
expr_long <- target_rows %>%
  # Swap the dataset's gene ID for the short label (REM16 / FT1) used in plots.
  mutate(gene = names(target_genes)[match(gene_id, target_genes)]) %>%
  select(-gene_id) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -gene,           # every column except gene is a sample
    names_to  = "sample_id",
    values_to = "expression"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Plant sex is encoded in the sample name suffix.
    sex = case_when(
      str_ends(sample_id, "_XX") ~ "Female (XX)",
      str_ends(sample_id, "_XY") ~ "Male (XY)"
      # anything else becomes NA and is removed below
    ),
    # Fix the factor order so females always plot first, and keep genes in
    # the order REM16, FT1 (factor() would otherwise sort alphabetically).
    sex  = factor(sex,  levels = names(sex_colors)),
    gene = factor(gene, levels = names(target_genes))
  )

# Data-quality step: drop samples with no recognised sex or a missing
# expression value, and report how many were removed so nothing vanishes silently.
n_before  <- nrow(expr_long)
expr_long <- expr_long %>% filter(!is.na(sex), !is.na(expression))
message("Removed ", n_before - nrow(expr_long), " of ", n_before,
        " gene-by-sample values (unrecognised sex or missing expression).")

# Final sanity check: print the sample size per gene and sex.
expr_long %>% count(gene, sex)
```

## 5. Plots

```{r plots}
# REM16 and FT1 plots are identical except for the gene, so we define the plot
# once as a function instead of copy-pasting the code.
plot_gene_by_sex <- function(gene_name) {
  expr_long %>%
    filter(gene == gene_name) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = sex, y = expression, fill = sex)) +
    # outlier.shape = NA hides the boxplot's own outlier dots because every
    # sample is already drawn by geom_jitter below (avoids double-plotting).
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +  # shows individual samples
    scale_fill_manual(values = sex_colors) +
    labs(title = paste(gene_name, "expression by plant sex"),
         x = "Plant sex", y = "Expression") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")  # x-axis already labels the sexes
}

p_rem16 <- plot_gene_by_sex("REM16")
p_ft1   <- plot_gene_by_sex("FT1")

# Combined plot: genes on the x-axis, sexes side by side within each gene.
# position_dodge / position_jitterdodge use the same dodge.width so the
# jittered points line up with their boxes.
p_combined <- ggplot(expr_long, aes(x = gene, y = expression, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
               outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
    size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_colors, name = "Plant sex") +
  labs(title = "REM16 and FT1 expression by plant sex",
       x = "Gene", y = "Expression") +
  theme_minimal()

p_rem16
p_ft1
p_combined
```

## 6. Save figures

```{r save}
# recursive = TRUE creates parent folders if needed; showWarnings = FALSE
# keeps quiet when the folder already exists (git does not track empty folders,
# so it will not exist in a fresh clone).
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "rem16_by_sex.png"),    p_rem16,    width = 4, height = 4, dpi = 300)
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "ft1_by_sex.png"),      p_ft1,      width = 4, height = 4, dpi = 300)
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "combined_by_sex.png"), p_combined, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)

message("Figures saved to: ", output_dir)
```

```{r session-info}

sessionInfo()
```
